newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan sees 30 pct GDP growth 1993-1998.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan sees 30 pct GDP growth 1993-1998.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan was quoted in a published report as saying gross domestic product should grow by close to 30 percent between 1993 and 1998.

This represents a "rupture with the previous 12 years, 1981 to 1992, when GDP per capita fell and inflation rose from 100 percent to 2,000 percent a year", the financial newspaper Gazeta Mercantil quoted him as saying.
Malan said this year's inflation rate was the lowest Brazil had seen since 1957, and next year's rate was on its way to being single-digit.
"Meanwhile, the idea that things could be derailed any moment continues," Gazeta quoted him as saying. "Basically this is a lack of faith in ourselves."
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom 5521 507 4151
